20.name: Improper Input Validation
20.dev_explain: The code trusts input without checking its shape, type, or bounds before using it. Fix: validate/whitelist input at the boundary before it touches business logic.

22.name: Path Traversal
22.dev_explain: A file path is built from user input without stripping '../' or resolving to a safe base directory, so an attacker can read/write files outside the intended folder. Fix: use File.expand_path + a strict prefix check, or a whitelist of allowed filenames.

77.name: Command Injection
77.dev_explain: User input reaches a command interpreter (shell, system call, or a method that builds one internally). An attacker can inject extra commands or arguments. Fix: don't build commands from user input; if unavoidable, use the array form of system()/Open3 so no shell is invoked, and whitelist the input.

78.name: OS Command Injection
78.dev_explain: User input flows into a shell command (system, backticks, %x{}, IO.popen). An attacker can append ';' or '|' to run arbitrary commands. Fix: avoid shelling out with user data; if unavoidable, use the array form of system() so no shell is invoked.

79.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
79.dev_explain: User-controlled data is rendered into HTML/JS without escaping (often via html_safe, raw, or unescaped ERB). Fix: let Rails auto-escape by default, and never wrap untrusted data in raw/html_safe.

88.name: Argument Injection
88.dev_explain: User input is passed as an argument to a command or API in a way that lets an attacker inject extra flags/arguments. Fix: use parameterized/array-style calls, never string-interpolated argument lists.

89.name: SQL Injection
89.dev_explain: A SQL query is built by interpolating user input directly into the query string instead of using bind parameters. Fix: use ActiveRecord parameterized finders (where("x = ?", val)) instead of string interpolation.

94.name: Code Injection
94.dev_explain: User input reaches eval, send, constantize, or similar dynamic-execution calls, letting an attacker run arbitrary Ruby code. Fix: never eval user input; use explicit whitelists/case statements instead of dynamic dispatch.

200.name: Information Exposure
200.dev_explain: The response leaks internal details (stack traces, file paths, secrets, other users' data) that aren't needed by the caller. Fix: return generic error messages in production and scope queries/serializers to only what the current user should see.

209.name: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
209.dev_explain: Raw exception messages/stack traces are shown to the end user, which can reveal internals attackers can use for follow-on attacks. Fix: rescue and log the real error server-side; show a generic message to the client.

259.name: Hard-coded Password
259.dev_explain: A credential is baked into source code. Fix: move it to environment variables / a secrets manager and rotate the exposed value.

284.name: Improper Access Control
284.dev_explain: The endpoint doesn't verify the current user is allowed to perform the action on the target resource. Fix: add an authorization check (e.g., current_user.owns?(resource) or a policy object) before acting.

295.name: Improper Certificate Validation
295.dev_explain: TLS certificate verification is disabled or weakened (e.g., OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE), so the app can be MITM'd. Fix: always verify certificates; only disable in isolated test environments.

306.name: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
306.dev_explain: A sensitive action is reachable without confirming who the caller is. Fix: require authentication (before_action :authenticate_user!) on the controller/action.

327.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
327.dev_explain: The code uses a weak/legacy algorithm (MD5, SHA1, DES) for something security-sensitive. Fix: use bcrypt for passwords and SHA-256+ (or a vetted library) for hashing/integrity needs.

352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
352.dev_explain: A state-changing action can be triggered by a form/request from another origin because CSRF protection is disabled or the token isn't checked. Fix: keep protect_from_forgery enabled and don't skip it for state-changing actions.

470.name: Unsafe Reflection (RCE via dynamic dispatch)
470.dev_explain: User input is passed to constantize, send, public_send, or similar reflection methods, letting an attacker instantiate arbitrary classes or call arbitrary methods — often a straight path to remote code execution. Fix: replace dynamic dispatch on user input with an explicit whitelist/case statement mapping allowed values to classes/methods.

434.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
434.dev_explain: The upload endpoint doesn't restrict file type/size/content, so an attacker can upload an executable or oversized file. Fix: whitelist content types/extensions, cap size, and store uploads outside the web root with a re-generated filename.

489.name: Active Debug Code
489.dev_explain: Debugging aids (binding.pry, console access, verbose logging) are reachable in production. Fix: strip debug entry points from production builds/config.

502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
502.dev_explain: User-controlled data is passed to Marshal.load, YAML.load, or similar, which can execute arbitrary code during deserialization. Fix: use YAML.safe_load or a data-only format like JSON for anything touching user input.

601.name: Open Redirect
601.dev_explain: redirect_to uses a user-supplied URL/param without validating it stays within the app, letting attackers use your domain to redirect to phishing sites. Fix: validate the target against a whitelist of internal paths/hosts.

611.name: XML External Entity Reference (XXE)
611.dev_explain: The XML parser resolves external entities from user-supplied XML, which can read local files or hit internal services. Fix: disable DTD/external entity processing on the parser (e.g., Nokogiri::XML::ParseOptions::NONET, no NOENT).

640.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism
640.dev_explain: The password-reset flow uses a guessable/non-expiring token or leaks whether an account exists. Fix: use a cryptographically random, single-use, time-limited token and a generic 'if that account exists' response.

732.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
732.dev_explain: A sensitive file/resource is created with overly permissive access. Fix: set the least-privileged file mode/ownership needed.

777.name: Regular Expression without Anchors
777.dev_explain: A validation regex is missing ^/$ anchors (or uses \A/\z incorrectly), so input like "valid-value\nmalicious payload" can slip past the check. Fix: anchor with \A and \z (not ^/$, which match line boundaries in Ruby) for full-string validation.

915.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes (Mass Assignment)
915.dev_explain: A model accepts a hash of attributes from the request and assigns them all, including ones the caller shouldn't be able to set (e.g. admin, role, account_id). Fix: use strong parameters (params.require(...).permit(:only, :allowed, :fields)) and never permit! wholesale.

1004.name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
1004.dev_explain: The session cookie can be read by JavaScript, so an XSS bug elsewhere becomes full session theft. Fix: ensure the session store config sets httponly: true (and secure: true over HTTPS).

1104.name: Use of Unmaintained Third-Party Component
1104.dev_explain: A dependency (or the Ruby/Rails version itself) is past end-of-life and no longer receives security patches. Fix: plan an upgrade — this is the SAST-side signal that lines up with Dependabot's SCA alerts for the same package.

798.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
798.dev_explain: A secret key, API token, or password is committed in source rather than pulled from configuration. Fix: rotate the exposed credential and load it from ENV/secrets manager instead.

807.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
807.dev_explain: A security-relevant decision (auth, redirect target, price, role) trusts a client-controlled value (hidden field, cookie, param) instead of server-side state. Fix: recompute or verify the value server-side; never trust the client for it.

862.name: Missing Authorization
862.dev_explain: The endpoint checks that a user is logged in but not that they're allowed to touch this specific resource (classic IDOR/insecure direct object reference). Fix: scope lookups to current_user (current_user.things.find(id)) rather than Model.find(id).

863.name: Incorrect Authorization
863.dev_explain: An authorization check exists but has a logic flaw (wrong role check, inverted condition) that lets it be bypassed. Fix: re-derive the check from the intended access-control rule and add a spec for the bypass case.

916.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
916.dev_explain: Passwords are hashed with a fast/unsalted algorithm instead of a slow, salted one. Fix: use bcrypt (has_secure_password) with a cost factor appropriate for production.

918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
918.dev_explain: The server fetches a URL supplied by the user, which can be pointed at internal-only services (metadata endpoints, admin panels). Fix: whitelist allowed hosts/schemes before making the outbound request.
